submission.summary: This 32-year-old man has had recurrent emergency presentations for motorcycle-related trauma and a high-pressure paint-gun injury. At his most recent ED visit (July 2021), a motorcycle accident was followed by right arm and leg weakness (3/5), impaired right-sided proprioception, vibration, and light touch, and diminished left-sided pain and temperature sensation below approximately T12, without reported bowel or bladder incontinence. Spinal MRI showed a right hemicord lesion at T10, consistent with a traumatic Brown-Séquard–type syndrome; CBC and electrolytes were normal and toxicology was negative. In January 2020, another motorcycle accident caused left leg pain, pallor, swelling, weak distal pulses, sensory and motor deficits, and Doppler-confirmed acute arterial occlusion treated with embolectomy; CK was 2,500 U/L, myoglobin 150 ng/mL, potassium 5.2 mEq/L, and creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, raising concern for muscle injury and compartment syndrome. His surgical history also records right hand fasciotomy for crush-related compartment syndrome. In July 2020, a workplace high-pressure paint injection into the left palm produced severe pain disproportionate to a small puncture wound, swelling, and pain on passive finger extension; hand radiographs showed no bony injury, WBC was 12,000/µL, and creatinine was 1.0 mg/dL. No chronic medical conditions or current medications are documented, and he has no known drug allergies. He is a former smoker, drinks alcohol socially, and works as an automotive spray painter.

This 28-year-old woman has hidradenitis suppurativa, diagnosed after recurrent painful axillary and groin nodules and abscesses with sinus tracts, and uses clindamycin 1% gel twice daily for HS and acne. She was subsequently evaluated by Dermatology for progressive crown hair thinning, with concurrent facial hirsutism and a history of acne. These androgen-associated findings occur in the setting of polycystic ovary syndrome, irregular menses, prior infertility and obesity (documented BMI 32–36 kg/m²); examination also showed cervical acanthosis nigricans. Total testosterone was elevated at 82 ng/dL, while TSH (2.1–2.5 µIU/mL), prolactin, fasting glucose (96–98 mg/dL) and lipid profile were normal. She takes metformin 1,000 mg twice daily for PCOS and was pregnant in 2023, an important consideration for systemic dermatologic treatment. Other relevant history includes irritable bowel syndrome, recurrent UTIs on daily nitrofurantoin prophylaxis, prior cholecystectomy, sphincter of Oddi dysfunction and acute cholangitis; in October 2023 she developed jaundice with marked transaminitis (AST 850, ALT 920 U/L, bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL), relevant to medication selection. Her other listed medications are a prenatal vitamin and as-needed dicyclomine; she is a former smoker, reports no alcohol use and has no known drug allergies.
